content.text: Game work on the main thread
content.help: Our game / menu / scene changes run on the game's main thread between frames (where console commands run). 0 = F4SE's task queue (any thread) and polls at Present, as before 20 Nov.

When the GPU is the bottleneck, wait for it before the next head pose is predicted, so frames are not drawn with a pose meant for an earlier display time (laggy / unstable head under GPU load). No wait when the GPU keeps up.
Frames still unfinished on the GPU when the next head pose is predicted. 1 = default; 0 = lowest latency, lower frame rate when GPU-bound; 2 = more frame rate headroom, more latency.

content.text: Full frame rate without window focus
content.help: High FPS Physics Fix limits the game to 60 fps (its OutOfFocusFPS) whenever another window has the focus, and the headset then gets 60 fps too. On: the game window does not report losing focus while the VR session runs.

content.text: GPU queue 0: relax when frames are late
content.help: Only with 'GPU frames queued at most' = 0. While frames miss the display period the wait for the GPU only costs frame rate, so 1 frame may be queued until CPU + GPU fit the period again. Changes head-pose timing while relaxed.
Each eye's part of the frame is copied straight into the headset's image (1 copy instead of 3 full-size passes per eye). Off = the previous path.
The game window on the desktop is only a mirror. 1 = updated every frame; 3 = every third frame (a little GPU time back; a recording of the window gets a third of the frames).
NVIDIA DLSS at native resolution per eye, in place of the game's TAA (the TAA cut is lifted while it runs). 0 = the game's TAA / bCutTaa as before.
0 = one shared instance over both eyes (test: one history over the double-wide image).

Sent at creation (DLSS accepts every mode at the eye size; measured 20 Nov). The input stays at the eye size: rendering below it is not part of this build. A mode DLSS refuses falls back to DLAA (logged).

The game's TAA camera jitter stays on so DLSS gets sub-pixel detail. 0 = no jitter (TAA stays active for DLSS).

ROCK's hands grab, pull and catch objects (grip). Off: no new grab starts and the grip goes back to the game; a held object stays until released. Live.
Weapon collision, two-handed support grip (a full-authority grip moves the gun), the weapon-held hand switch and the grip alignment. Off: ROCK sees no weapon. Live.

Swing the held weapon (gun bash too) or the bare hand into an actor and the game's melee hit lands on it (FO4VR). Live.
Hand speed a swing needs to hit (FO4VR 200). Live.
Or this wrist turn speed (FO4VR 1.0 rad/s = 10). Live.
As FO4VR: with a melee weapon or fists drawn the trigger does not swing; hold it while swinging for a power attack. Live.
Grab a gun from the world and pull that hand's trigger: it becomes your weapon (silently, as FO4VR ROCK). Live.
As FO4VR with ROCK: tap B = V.A.T.S., hold B = a grenade drawn into your hand to throw. The grip-hold grenade throw stays. Live.
As FO4VR: a gun equipped from the left hand stays in the left hand as the firing hand (its trigger fires). Live.

content.text: Gun keeps its aim at walls
content.help: The held gun pushed against a wall slides back along its aim instead of twisting (ROCK's soft contact response turned the gun 40-98 deg). 0 = ROCK's own response. Live.

With [Controllers] bLeftHanded=1 ROCK's default firing hand is the left (FO4VR: ROCK FiringHand.DefaultHand=left): the grenade goes to the free right hand, the left trigger fires, the right trigger stays the Pip-Boy's; the hand switch works from the left (grip the handle with the right hand, let go with the left: the right trigger then fires). 0 = ROCK's own DefaultHand. Live.
ROCK-flat diagnostic lines in ROCK.log (grip press, squeeze, release, hand-switch zone, input, frame time). Live.
